claims.text: Pulumi prints placeholder text like `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` in log lines, generated files, or resource properties when an Output is treated as if it were a plain value.
A page titled 'Output value errors' exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ and covers this and other symptoms of treating an output as if it were already a plain value.
The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ exists and covers diagnosing errors from stringifying, branching on, or reading a Pulumi output value like a plain value.
The link target /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ exists in the Pulumi docs.
Stringifying, branching on, or reading a Pulumi output value like a plain value produces errors in Pulumi programs.
Pulumi Cloud returns a "409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress" error on update conflicts, documented at the update-conflicts troubleshooting page.
Pulumi Cloud can return 500 internal server errors.
The CLI produces `read ".pulumi/meta.yaml"` errors when it can't access a self-managed (DIY) state backend, and the using-a-diy-backend page has an anchor #error-reading-pulumimetayaml.
On Apple Silicon Macs, running x86_64 binaries under Rosetta 2 can cause crashes or hangs with Pulumi.
A recently deleted stack can be recovered from the Pulumi Cloud console, including after an accidental `pulumi stack rm --force`.
Pulumi CLI supports `--target` and `--exclude` flags to limit operations to specific resources.
Running `pulumi logs share` securely sends the logs from a failed operation to the Pulumi team.
Pulumi dev builds are pre-release builds that provide bug fixes not yet shipped in a stable release.
Pulumi provides automatic logging, CLI verbose logging, and program logging for debugging.
Pulumi offers a Community Slack at slack.pulumi.com and paid support options.
Pulumi resource properties are represented as Outputs rather than plain values because their real values are not known until the providing resource has been created or updated.

When an Output value is converted to a string directly (concatenated, logged) instead of via apply, Pulumi does not raise an error by default but silently substitutes a placeholder message for the value.
In Pulumi TypeScript, converting an Output to a string yields text such as `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `apply` or `pulumi.interpolate`.
In Pulumi TypeScript, calling `JSON.stringify()` on an Output produces a `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` string rather than the value.
In Pulumi Python, using an Output in an f-string yields text such as `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported` and Pulumi also logs a warning, without raising an exception.
In Pulumi Python, passing an Output to `json.dumps()` fails with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`; `Output.json_dumps()` should be used instead.
In Pulumi Go, passing a `pulumi.StringOutput` where a `string` is expected is a compile error; values are resolved inside `ApplyT`.
In Pulumi C#, converting an Output to a string yields text such as `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `Apply` or `Output.Format`.

Setting the environment variable `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true` (supported in TypeScript, Python, and C#) makes converting an Output to a string throw an exception instead of returning the placeholder text.

Pulumi string-composition helpers: `pulumi.interpolate` and `pulumi.concat` in TypeScript, `Output.concat`/`Output.format`/`Output.json_dumps` in Python, `pulumi.Sprintf`/`pulumi.JSONMarshal` in Go, and `Output.Format` in C#.

The `apply` callback runs asynchronously once the output resolves, generally after the program's top-level code has finished, so reading an outer variable assigned inside the callback yields `undefined`.
Most Pulumi resource inputs accept outputs as well as plain values, while a handful of positions such as a resource's logical name cannot.

In dynamically typed languages, an `if` on a Pulumi Output evaluates the Output object rather than its eventual value and is generally always true; in statically typed languages it is usually a compile error because `Output<bool>` is not `bool`.
Values known at program start, such as stack configuration read with `pulumi.Config`, environment variables, or hardcoded flags, are plain values and can be branched on normally.
Passing an Output as a resource's logical name or loop bound fails to compile in TypeScript, Go, and C#.
In Pulumi Python, passing an Output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string`.
In Python, using an Output as a loop bound (`range(some_output)`) raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`.
In Python, using a Pulumi Output as a dictionary key does not raise; it silently keys on the Output object itself rather than its resolved value.
A StackReference lets a later, separate stack consume the first stack's outputs; the link target /docs/iac/concepts/stacks/#stackreferences exists.

Pulumi has no supported way to block the program and synchronously pull a resolved value out of an Output; awaiting or synchronously reading an output either doesn't compile, fails at runtime, or returns placeholder text.
`pulumi stack output <name>` reads a single stack output from the CLI after a deployment.
The Automation API exposes an `outputs` field on the result of running an update (for example `res.Outputs` in Go).

Cross-referenced pages exist: /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/, /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/apply/, /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/all/, /docs/iac/concepts/stacks/#stackreferences, /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/.
